items.title: Arbitrary-rank Coxeter presentations, length, reflections, and Bruhat order
items.statement: Extend the local finite-generator Coxeter presentation and reflection-chain Bruhat conventions to an arbitrary generator set S; define word length and reduced expressions without asserting unproved parabolic or subword properties.
items.strategy: Give the presentation, length, reflection set, and reflection-chain order as definitions; identify the finite-S specialization with the existing local convention.
items.axiom_use: None; the construction is a quotient presentation and a least natural length.

items.title: Canonical basic sets for split Hecke specializations
items.statement: Define decomposition numbers, the minimum alpha value of a modular simple, and the two triangularity conditions that characterize a canonical basic set relative to a chosen integer statistic alpha on generic irreducibles.
items.strategy: State the finite-Weyl split modular system and reproduce the canonical-basic-set conditions; make no existence claim.
items.axiom_use: None; this is a definition using a supplied decomposition matrix and integer statistic.

items.title: Schur elements of a split semisimple algebra with a symmetrizing trace
items.statement: Define the Schur elements associated with a symmetrizing trace on a split semisimple algebra by its irreducible-character expansion, without asserting existence outside the explicit cases computed locally.
items.strategy: Specify the split algebra, its trace and characters, and define the nonzero coefficients in the trace expansion as Schur elements.

items.title: Lusztig P1–P15 are not universally proved cell properties
items.statement: Record that P1–P15 are explicitly conjectural in Lusztig’s bounded setup and that the local basis and cell-module results prove none of them.
items.strategy: State the exact source status, boundedness hypothesis, and local theorem boundary without making a classification claim.

sources.locator: §13.1–13.2 and §14.1–14.3, PDF pp. 55–58: boundedness and the explicit conjecture status of P1–P15.

items.title: Complete local modular systems and integral idempotent lifting
Weight functions and ordered group-algebra coefficients
items.statement: Define weight functions L:W→Γ into a totally ordered abelian group, the group algebra A=Z[Γ], its bar involution, and the strictly negative coefficient part; no sign restriction is imposed on L(s).
items.strategy: Specify Γ, A, bar, A_<0, and length-additivity for L; a separate lemma proves the exact odd-edge criterion for generator labels.
items.axiom_use: None; no choice axiom is used.

items.title: Finite-generator standard parabolics and the Bruhat subword property at arbitrary rank
items.statement: For arbitrary S, every finite J⊂S presents an embedded standard parabolic with intrinsic length equal to ambient length; the global reflection-chain Bruhat order has the reduced-subword characterization and finite lower intervals.
items.strategy: Build the geometric action on the free vector space on S by consistent finite restrictions, use finite-generator faithfulness to embed each finite presentation, then reduce every word, chain, and Bruhat comparison to a finite support set.
items.axiom_use: None; all supports and chains are finite and the construction is explicit.

items.title: Simple-generator weights extend uniquely to a weight function
items.statement: A map L:W→Γ is a weight function exactly when its simple-generator labels are constant on every finite odd-labelled edge; such labels extend uniquely to L.
items.strategy: Define L(w) by summing labels along a reduced expression, reduce comparisons to a finite parabolic and check braid moves; compare the two odd dihedral longest words for necessity.
items.axiom_use: None; every expression and braid sequence is finite.

items.title: The unequal-parameter Coxeter Hecke algebra
items.statement: Define H_A(W,L) by the symmetric quadratic relation (T_s−v^{L(s)})(T_s+v^{−L(s)})=0 and the Coxeter braid relations over A=Z[Γ].
items.strategy: State the generator-and-relation presentation and the parameter and bar conventions without asserting a basis until the following theorem.

items.title: The arbitrary-rank weighted Hecke basis and Bruhat-triangular bar
items.statement: For arbitrary-rank (W,S), the elements T_w form an A-basis; bar is a well-defined semilinear involution with bar(T_s)=T_s^{-1}, and bar(T_w)−T_w is supported on y<w, for every weight function L.
items.strategy: Apply the existing finite-generator standard-basis theorem to finite standard parabolics, prove global spanning and independence by finite support, verify bar on the presentation, and expand its inverse-word formula using the subword theorem.
items.axiom_use: None; every element, relation, and word has finite support.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the ordered-group unequal-parameter Kazhdan–Lusztig basis
items.statement: For any weight function into a totally ordered abelian group, there is a unique bar-invariant family C_w=T_w+Σ_{y<w}p_{y,w}T_y with p_{y,w}∈A_<0; it is an A-basis.
items.strategy: Use finite Bruhat intervals and triangular induction; split each anti-invariant coefficient into its strictly negative part.
items.axiom_use: None; each lower interval is finite and every coefficient has finite support.

items.statement: Define the left, right, and two-sided KL preorders from nonzero generator-action coefficients, their cell equivalence classes, and the corresponding filtered quotient spaces.
items.strategy: State the structure-constant relations and define each cell quotient; the following theorem proves the ideal and module properties.
items.axiom_use: None; all structure-constant expansions are finite.

items.title: Finite-Weyl Lusztig data and the precise basic-set hypotheses
Weighted cell quotients are well-defined modules and bimodules
items.statement: For every weighted Coxeter Hecke algebra, the lower-cell spans are left, right, or two-sided ideals as appropriate; the cell quotients are left modules, right modules, or bimodules with cell-indexed bases.
items.strategy: Prove closure under each C_s action from the generating coefficient relations and transitivity of the preorders; use T_s=C_s−v^{−L(s)} to pass to the full Hecke algebra.
items.axiom_use: None; the argument uses only finite algebra products and finite chains.

items.title: The asymptotic algebra, filtered layers and the specialization homomorphism
The four weighted cells of A1×A1 give a canonical basic set at odd residue characteristic
items.statement: For W=A1×A1 with L(s)=1,L(t)=2, O=Z_p for any odd prime p, and v=1+p, the four weighted cell characters reduce to four distinct simple modules; their decomposition matrix is the identity, so they form the canonical basic set for any alpha statistic.
items.strategy: Compute the four KL cell modules, split both rank-one factors by explicit integral idempotents, reduce modulo p, and verify the defining triangularity conditions directly.
items.axiom_use: None; all algebras, idempotents, modules, and reductions are explicit and finite.

items.statement: Refute the assertion that all four distinct generic A1×A1 weighted cell-module labels remain distinct after every modular specialization.
